target: Eles misturam português com inglês.
tip: Language names stay lowercase in Portuguese: português and inglês are never capitalized.

target: Eu conheço bem esse bairro.
tip: 'Conhecer' means to know in the sense of being familiar with a place or person. 'Saber' is for knowing facts or how to do something.

target: Você mistura os ingredientes devagar.
tip: devagar means slowly and is already an adverb, so it never takes the -mente ending.

target: Ele comenta nas redes sociais.
tip: nas is em plus as (in or on the, feminine plural): nas redes sociais.

target: Eu pego trânsito todo dia.
tip: 'Pegar trânsito' is a very Brazilian expression meaning to get stuck in traffic. 'Pegar' is one of the most versatile verbs in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Ele está no escritório agora.
tip: Use estar, not ser, for where someone is right now: está no escritório places him at the office at this moment.

target: Ela tem preguiça de cozinhar.
tip: 'Ter preguiça de' means 'to feel lazy about' – yet another common 'ter' expression for states and feelings.

target: Eu posso trazer um amigo?
tip: trazer is to bring toward you, here: posso trazer um amigo. Use levar instead for taking something away from where you are.

target: Ele faz falta na equipe.
tip: fazer falta means to be missed: ele faz falta = the team misses him. Literally it means to make lack.

target: Muito prazer em conhecer você.
tip: conhecer is to meet someone for the first time or to know a person, not to know a fact.

target: Eles gostam de churrasco no domingo.
tip: Sunday churrasco (barbecue) is a sacred Brazilian tradition – it's the main social gathering of the week for most families.

target: A gente agenda tudo pelo WhatsApp.
tip: a gente (literally "the people") = informal nós (we). Conjugates as 3rd singular: a gente vai (not a gente vamos). Brazilians say this all the time.

target: Ela corrige os textos dos alunos.
tip: Portuguese has no apostrophe-s. Show possession with de: os textos dos alunos = the students' texts.

target: Eu tenho dois irmãos mais velhos.
tip: irmãos is masculine plural but can mean siblings of mixed gender, not only brothers.

target: A gente tem que sair agora.
tip: 'Ter que' + infinitive means 'to have to.' It's the most common way to express obligation in Brazilian Portuguese, more than 'dever.'

target: Ele diz que vai chegar atrasado.
tip: dizer is irregular: eu digo, ele diz. Here diz means says.

target: Eu quero um café, por favor.
tip: quero um café is perfectly polite in Portuguese; add por favor and it carries none of the bluntness English 'I want' would.

target: Ela está trabalhando de casa hoje.
tip: estar plus an -ndo verb marks an action in progress: está trabalhando is 'she is working' right now.

target: Nós somos amigos desde a infância.
tip: desde marks a starting point in time, meaning since: desde a infância = since childhood.

target: Boa tarde, como vão as coisas?
tip: como vão as coisas uses vão (they go) to ask how things are going.

target: Nós dissemos tchau e fomos embora.
tip: 'Ir embora' means to leave or go away, not just to go somewhere: 'fomos embora' = we left.

target: Eu fui embora sem me despedir.
tip: 'Sem' followed by an infinitive means without doing something: 'sem me despedir' = without saying goodbye.

target: Eu carrego o celular durante a noite.
tip: carregar means both to charge a device and to carry: carrego o celular = I charge my phone.

target: O jornal de hoje traz boas notícias.
tip: trazer (to bring) is irregular: eu trago, ele traz. Here traz = brings.

target: Eu pego o trem das sete e meia.
tip: 'Trem' is the Brazilian word for train. In Portugal, they say 'comboio.'

target: A gente está com vontade de comer pizza.
tip: 'Estar com vontade de' means 'to feel like doing something.' It's the natural way Brazilians express cravings and desires.

target: Eu costumo dormir cedo.
english: I usually go to sleep early.
tip: 'Costumar' + infinitive means 'to usually do something.' It's the most natural way to express habits in Portuguese.

target: Ela sabe tocar piano.
english: She knows how to play piano.
tip: tocar is to play an instrument. For sports and games use jogar instead.

target: Eles jogam vôlei na praia.
english: They play volleyball at the beach.
tip: Use jogar for sports and games: jogam vôlei. Musical instruments take tocar instead.

target: Ele passa roupa de manhã.
english: He irons clothes in the morning.
tip: passar roupa means to iron clothes, literally to pass clothes.
